newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car stocks boosted by Italian sales rise.
newsitem.headline: French car stocks boosted by Italian sales rise.

text.p: French car stocks rose on Wednesday, helped by a 50.7 percent surge in June car sales in Italy, a major market for the French car industry, brokers said.
Valeo, which reported a 14.6 percent rise in first-half sales and reports first-half results next week, closed up 4.49 percent higher at 414.50 francs.
PSA Peugeot Citroen, which introduced the Citroen ZX replacement, the new Xsara, rose 2.94 percent to 596 francs.
Renault gained 1.67 percent to 146.10 francs after Vilvoorde unions approved the plan for the Belgian plant closure, adding another ray of good news in a sector wrapped in gloom recently.
Michelin shares rose 2.18 percent to 385 francs.
Car sales in Italy rose 50.71 percent in June and were up 31 percent for the first half of the year, helped by a buying incentive scheme.

"Everybody looks at the French car sales but the French carmakers export a lot -- three-quarters of Peugeot's five-month sales were exports -- and their turnover isn't too bad. Further, the foreign exchange trends are very favourable," said Philippe Barrier at brokerage SGE Delahaye.
He said some specialists expect the downturn in the French market since the end of incentives last September to end with the start of the new model year this month.
